items.title: Jack Lesberg interviewed by Monk Rowe, Aspen, Colorado, October 11, 1997
items.q: they called him “Pete Pesky” or something like that. And all the way through this he’s playing the trombone.

ctx.x: Condon wasn’t known for his soloing but he certainly was a catalyst.

Oh, yeah, oh he was a terrific catalyst, yeah. And he was fun. He wasn’t a great player or anything, but he did have — there are certain things that he enjoyed and they were great jazz things, like having people like Lee Wiley as one of the singers, and having, he had Louis Armstrong on the program, and Jack Teagarden I think was recording for some company and they couldn’t use his name and so they called him “Pete Pesky” or something like that. And all the way through this he’s playing the trombone. And Ernie…
